note_on_H_symbol: The chapter on Columns/Walls/Foundations/Staircases (pp.88-127) uses 'H' throughout as the bar-type symbol (e.g. '4 H20', 'H10 U-bars') for high-yield deformed bar. This appendix's explicit symbol list (R/T/X/S/W/D/F/B) does not include 'H'. INFERRED: 'H' is very likely the BS8666/Eurocode-era standard symbol for high-yield deformed reinforcement (in common UK practice, H = high yield deformed, replacing T), but this extract does not directly state that mapping, so it is NOT to be treated as DIRECTLY STATED.

bar_shape_code_catalogue.constraints: No other shape code, designation, or abbreviation permitted; sketch must be dimensioned A-E with the tolerance-absorbing dimension in parentheses; otherwise fabricator chooses

general_notes_all_shape_codes: Values for minimum radius (r) and end dimension (A), per Table B.1, apply to all shape codes.

Dimensions in parentheses are free dimensions (absorb permissible deviation). If a different dimension must absorb tolerance than the one shown in parentheses for a standard shape, the shape must be redrawn and coded 99, with the actual free dimension shown in parentheses.
Minimum straight length between two bends: at least 4d (see BS8666 Figure 6).
BS8666 Figures 4, 5, 6 should be used to interpret bending dimensions (external reference, not reproduced here).

Note 1: Length equations for shapes 14, 15, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 34, 35, 36, 46 are approximate; where bend angle > 45deg, length should be calculated more accurately (true centreline length vs specified overall dims differ); near 90deg bends, prefer shape code 99 with a fully dimensioned sketch.
Note 2: 5 or more bends may be impractical within permitted tolerances.
Note 3: For shapes with straight + curved lengths (12, 13, 22, 33, 47), largest practical mandrel size for a continuous curve is 400mm (see BS8666 Clause 10).

Note 4: Stock lengths available in a limited number of lengths (e.g. 6m, 12m). Dimension A for shape code 01 is indicative; actual delivery length by agreement with supplier; tolerances per relevant product standard (e.g. BS449:2005 cited, likely a scan/OCR error for a different standard number — flagged in gaps).
